clue.text: Young people's songs deflate a character so

parts.note: to deflate a balloon is to pop it
mu is a character of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for so, or thus

explanation.surface: Some cruel teenage songs puncture a person's ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a character' looks like a person, but here it means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular chart music is the kind of song associated with the young, so this is a fair descriptive gloss.

clue.text: State of house kept by good monk

parts.note: OK means all right, good

indicators.note: a thing kept by something sits inside it, so the house goes inside the monk

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A monk of some virtue maintains a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Northeast Chinese fellow to agitate around outskirts of India

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the agitating word goes around the edge letters of India

parts.note: to churn is to stir or agitate

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man from China's northeast stirs up trouble on the fringes of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northeast Chinese' reads as a person, but it is the adjective; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchuria is the historical region in China's northeast, and the adjective describes a person or thing from there.

clue.text: Honestly, what can be said for scattered sheep?

indicators.note: a phrase about what is said, pointing to a sound-alike of the two words

parts.note: a stray (scattered, wandering) tup, a tup being a ram

explanation.surface: A farmer asks, in all honesty, what excuse can be made for the flock wandering off.
explanation.walkthrough: A TUP is a ram, a word common in British farming; STRAY TUP said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something straight up means saying it frankly and without evasion, which is to speak honestly.

clue.text: With clubs, I pitched into saint —— brute!

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the I is thrown into the middle of the saint's name

parts.note: St Alban was Britain's first Christian martyr

explanation.surface: Someone wielding clubs lashes out at a holy man and is denounced as a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: St ALBAN gives his name to the English city of St Albans.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the savage, monstrous servant in Shakespeare's The Tempest, a byword for a brute.

clue.text: Asian resettled in central Tahiti

indicators.note: letters resettled are moved into new places
the central part of a word is all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A traveller from Asia has made a new home in the heart of Tahiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes AHIT from Tahiti, and 'resettled' rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Pull off railway heist, run away (twice), to be secure?

indicators.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run, and it goes away from the word two times

parts.note: to carry out a railway heist is to rob a train

explanation.surface: A gang wonders whether robbing a train and fleeing twice will leave them safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Rs from ROB TRAIN to leave the answer. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to get hold of it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Narrow country adopts otherwise broad view

indicators.note: the country takes the other word into itself

parts.note: Panama is a thin isthmus country
or means otherwise, as in leave or else

explanation.surface: A slim nation takes up a different, wide-ranging outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Narrow' looks like a verb but describes Panama's thin shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view of a scene.

clue.text: Palace put support behind leaderless South London area

indicators.note: the supporting word goes after the other
a word without its leader loses its first letter

parts.note: Balham is a district of South London
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A palace has been propped up behind a South London neighbourhood that lacks a chief.
explanation.walkthrough: BALHAM is a district of south London; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace complex at Granada in Spain.

clue.text: Flat scheme with sharps in the middle

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: the middle pair of letters of the six-letter word is wanted

explanation.surface: A level arrangement of music has sharps placed in its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' and 'sharps' tempt a musical reading; flat is simply level here.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar means lying in a single plane, so flat in the geometric sense.

clue.text: A heartless lie leads to trouble for a fanatic

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle letter

parts.note: a fiction is an untruth
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A cruel falsehood stirs up strife that suits a zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes T, the middle letter of FICTION. 'leads to' and 'for a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen devotee or enthusiast, which is what fanatic means in its loose sense.

clue.text: Substitute for meat loaf finally accepted in almost all of France

indicators.note: the final letter is taken inside the shortened French word
almost means the word less its last letter

parts.note: tout is French for all

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A meat-free alternative to meat loaf is at last welcome across nearly all of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TOUT to TOU, and 'finally' gives F, the last letter of loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, made from soya bean curd, is widely used in place of meat in vegetarian cooking.

clue.text: Shuddering at and aping furry animal

indicators.note: shuddering shakes the following letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A creature shakes as it is mimicked at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AT, AND and APING are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear with a thick, furry coat.

clue.text: Twins start to tell yarn related to daughter

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: woof is the weft yarn in weaving
akin means related

explanation.surface: Twins begin telling a story about a girl in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story but is the weaving thread WOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of a kind is an idiom for a matching pair, which is what twins are.

clue.text: Version for TV of a feature to do with evolution

definitions.meaning: a novel or play reworked for television

definitions.text: a feature to do with evolution
definitions.meaning: a trait that suits an organism to its environment through natural selection

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a reworking of a story for another medium and an evolved trait suiting an organism to its surroundings.

clue.text: Attack on Italy is a failure

indicators.note: a failure suggests something has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An offensive against Italy collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ON and ITALY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is an idiom for attacking them, physically or verbally.

clue.text: See one's leader consumed by mounting passions, a reprobate

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: the leading letter is eaten up inside the other piece
in a down clue, mounting means read upwards

parts.note: lusts are strong passions

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Look how someone ruled by rising desires has become a degenerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns LUSTS into STSUL, and 'consumed by' places O, the first letter of one's, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost soul is a person beyond redemption, which is what a reprobate is.

clue.text: Bachelor supported by an unknown area's source of wealth

parts.note: on means resting upon, so supported by
Z is a mathematical unknown
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A single man is propped up by money from some unknown region.
explanation.walkthrough: The bachelor sits on what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a rich vein of ore, and hence any windfall or source of great wealth.

clue.text: Having to do with houses connected to Sky?

definitions.text: Having to do with houses connected to Sky?

parts.words: Having to do with houses connected to Sky?
parts.note: houses here are the twelve astrological divisions of the heavens, so the adjective concerns star signs rather than homes with satellite dishes

explanation.surface: Something about homes that subscribe to a satellite television service.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster, which makes the houses look like homes with dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Zodiacal means relating to the zodiac, whose twelve signs astrologers call houses of the sky.

clue.text: City visited by boat or on toboggan

indicators.note: the answer is visited by these words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A city where people arrive by boat or slide in on toboggans.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'boaT OR ON TOboggan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: Incontrovertible evidence keeping the racket inside?

parts.note: a sound argument cannot be refuted
proof is evidence

explanation.surface: Irrefutable evidence keeps the crooked scheme under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a fraud, but means noise, kept in by insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundproof room is insulated so noise made inside does not escape.

clue.text: Guardian relaxes when king and I leave country

indicators.note: relaxed letters loosen and settle in a new order
the named letters leave the word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A guardian unwinds once the monarch and the speaker have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes R and I out of GUARDIAN, leaving GUADAN for 'relaxes' to rearrange. 'The King and I' is a famous musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Neat as the ebb and flow?

definitions.meaning: like the tide, read as an adjective formed from tide

explanation.definitionFit: The word means orderly, and whimsically also tide-like, describing the rise and fall of the sea.

clue.text: Hit out in disagreement with director's preparation of The Birds?

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel

indicators.note: out means the named word is removed

parts.note: Alfred Hitchcock directed the film The Birds
taken as written, the three letters to remove

explanation.surface: A row with Hitchcock over how to film his famous thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Birds' looks like the film but means poultry. 'in' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatchcock a chicken is to split and flatten it for grilling, a way of preparing birds.

clue.text: Ultimately, Irish bull includes a joke

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word
the animal word takes the article inside it

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal like a bull

explanation.surface: In the end, an Irish bull, a self-contradictory statement, contains a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: An Irish bull is a laughably illogical statement, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a trick or practical joke.

clue.text: Inroad into country's borders — folly

indicators.note: borders are the outer edges, so each word gives its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advancing into a nation's frontiers is sheer foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' applies to all three words: Inroad gives ID, into gives IO, country gives CY. 'Inroad' wants to be an invasion; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy and folly are synonyms, both meaning foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Almost extreme viewpoint doesn't start fluctuating

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: undue means excessive or extreme

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a slant is an angle or point of view

explanation.surface: An almost radical outlook that never gets going keeps wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDUE less its last letter gives UNDU; SLANT less its first gives LANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Undulant means rising and falling in waves, so fluctuating.

clue.text: Figures indicating position of Rosalind, in disguise

indicators.note: a name in disguise has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Rosalind's place in the cast, while she is disguised as a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosalind disguises herself in Shakespeare's As You Like It, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers such as first and second show position in a sequence.
